subproblems.title: Dilation calculus: pull-back of test forms, push-forward of currents, commutation with ∂
subproblems.statement: Dilation calculus on ℝ^N (Simon Ch. 6, 2.23 and 2.24(1) for η_ρ(x) = ρx). Let N ∈ ℕ, ρ > 0 and k ∈ ℕ. Test forms are elements of TestFormOn univ (C^∞, compact support) and currents are elements of GeometricCurrentOn univ, on ℝ^N = Eucl N. Then: (1) for every test k-form ω there is a test k-form η with η(x) = ρ^k ω(ρx) for all x; (2) for every X ∈ D_k(ℝ^N) there is Y ∈ D_k(ℝ^N) with Y(ω) = X(η) for all test k-forms ω, η satisfying η(x) = ρ^k ω(ρx) for all x; (3) if X, Y ∈ D_{k+1}(ℝ^N) satisfy Y(ω) = X(η) for all test (k+1)-forms ω, η with η(x) = ρ^{k+1} ω(ρx) for all x, then ∂Y(ω) = ∂X(η) for all test k-forms ω, η with η(x) = ρ^k ω(ρx) for all x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (ρ : ℝ), 0 < ρ → ∀ k : ℕ, (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl N)) k, ∃ η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl N)) k, ∀ x, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl N) k) x = ρ ^ k • (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl N) k) (ρ • x)) ∧ (∀ X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl N)) k, ∃ Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl N)) k, (∀ ω η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl N)) k, (∀ x, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl N) k) x = ρ ^ k • (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl N) k) (ρ • x)) → Y ω = X η)) ∧ ∀ X Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl N)) (k + 1), (∀ ω η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl N)) (k + 1), (∀ x, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl N) (k + 1)) x = ρ ^ (k + 1) • (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl N) (k + 1)) (ρ • x)) → Y ω = X η) → ∀ ω η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl N)) k, (∀ x, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl N) k) x = ρ ^ k • (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl N) k) (ρ • x)) → Y.boundary ω = X.boundary η
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Notation and Steps 1, 2 and 9. These specialise Simon Ch. 6, 2.23 (push-forward f_#T(ω) = T(f^#ω) by a smooth proper map), 2.24(1) (∂f_#T = f_#∂T) and §1, 1.14 (pull-back commutes with d) to the dilation η_ρ(x) = ρx.

Conventions.
- ℝ^N := Eucl N.
- A j-form is a map ℝ^N → Covector (ℝ^N) j, i.e. into the continuous alternating j-linear maps.
- A test j-form is an element of TestFormOn univ j: a C^∞ form with compact support (tsupport ⊆ univ is automatic). Two test forms with the same underlying form are equal (Subtype.ext).
- Fix N, ρ > 0 and k, and let L := ρ • id : ℝ^N →L[ℝ] ℝ^N.
- For a j-form ω, L^#ω is the j-form x ↦ ω(Lx) ∘ (L, …, L), i.e. (L^#ω)(x)(v₁,…,v_j) = ω(ρx)(ρv₁,…,ρv_j).

Formalization note. L^#ω is SimonGMT's affinePullbackForm L 0 ω, from Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter06.AffineCurrentPushforward in the pinned simongmt package (rev 2b366308). That module is not in the import closure of the frozen contract. Add `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter06.AffineCurrentPushforward` at the top of GMT/Ch06/Submission.lean: the comparator byte-checks only the frozen files other than Submission.lean, and accepted nodes already add imports. Auxiliary lemmas need globally unique names, e.g. prefixed deformation_dilation_calculus_.

1. Scaling identity. For every j, every j-covector α and all v₁,…,v_j ∈ ℝ^N, α(ρv₁,…,ρv_j) = ρ^j·α(v₁,…,v_j), because α is linear in each of its j slots. For j = 0 the product of the factors is empty and ρ^0 = 1. Hence (L^#ω)(x) = ρ^j • ω(ρ • x) for every j-form ω and every x.
[Lean: ext v. Then (ω (ρ • x)).map_smul_univ (fun _ => ρ) v gives ω(ρx)(fun i => ρ • v i) = (∏ i : Fin j, ρ) • ω(ρx) v. Finset.prod_const, Finset.card_univ and Fintype.card_fin turn the product into ρ ^ j. Unfold affinePullbackForm with ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMap_apply, zero_add and Function.comp_def.]

2. L is proper. L is a homeomorphism of ℝ^N (its inverse is y ↦ ρ⁻¹y, since ρ ≠ 0), and homeomorphisms are proper maps.
[Lean: (fun x => 0 + L x) = ⇑(Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero ρ hρ.ne') by funext and simp; then Homeomorph.isProperMap.]

3. First conjunct. Let ω be a test k-form and put η := L^#ω.
(a) η is C^∞. The map x ↦ ω(Lx) is the composite of the C^∞ map ω with the linear map L. The map α ↦ α ∘ (L,…,L) is a continuous linear map on k-covectors.
(b) tsupport η ⊆ L⁻¹(tsupport ω). If ω vanishes on a neighbourhood V of Lx, then η vanishes on the neighbourhood L⁻¹(V) of x.
(c) tsupport ω is compact, so L⁻¹(tsupport ω) is compact by step 2. Hence the closed set tsupport η ⊆ L⁻¹(tsupport ω) is compact, and tsupport η ⊆ univ.
So η ∈ TestFormOn univ k, and η(x) = ρ^k • ω(ρ • x) for every x by step 1.
[Lean: η := affinePullbackTestOn L 0 hproper univ k ω, built from affinePullbackForm_isSmoothForm, tsupport_affinePullbackForm_subset and affinePullbackForm_isTestForm. Its type TestFormOn ((fun x => 0 + L x) ⁻¹' univ) k is definitionally TestFormOn univ k, since Set.preimage_univ is rfl. The pointwise identity is step 1.]

4. The pull-back operator. Let P : TestFormOn univ k → TestFormOn univ k be P ω := L^#ω (step 3).
(a) P is ℝ-linear: L^#(aω + bω′) = a·L^#ω + b·L^#ω′ pointwise.
(b) P is sequentially continuous at 0 for Simon's test-form topology. Suppose TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0. Then there is a compact K with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for all j, and for every i ∈ ℕ the i-th iterated derivatives D^iω_j converge uniformly on K to D^i0 = 0.
(i) tsupport(Pω_j) ⊆ L⁻¹(K) for all j by step 3(b), and L⁻¹(K) is a fixed compact set by step 2. Also tsupport(P0) = tsupport 0 = ∅ ⊆ L⁻¹(K).
(ii) By the chain rule, D^i(Pω_j)(x) = J_i(D^iω_j(Lx)). Here J_i is the fixed continuous linear map on i-jets that precomposes each of the i derivative slots and each of the k covector slots with L. For x ∈ L⁻¹(K) we have Lx ∈ K, and J_i is uniformly continuous. So D^i(Pω_j) → J_i(0) = 0 = D^i(P0) uniformly on L⁻¹(K).
Thus TestFormOnConverges (Pω_j) (P0), and P0 = 0.
[Lean: affinePullbackTestOn is a LinearMap; use iteratedFDeriv_affinePullbackForm and TestFormOnConverges.affinePullback.]

5. Second conjunct. Let X ∈ GeometricCurrentOn univ k and define Y := X ∘ P.
- Y is ℝ-linear, as a composite of linear maps.
- Continuity: if TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0, then TestFormOnConverges (Pω_j) 0 by step 4(b). So Y(ω_j) = X(Pω_j) → 0 by the continuity field of X. Hence Y ∈ GeometricCurrentOn univ k.
- Pair property: let ω, η be test k-forms with η(x) = ρ^k • ω(ρ • x) for all x. By step 1, η and Pω have the same underlying form. So η = Pω, and Y(ω) = X(Pω) = X(η).
[Lean: Y := GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward (V := univ) L 0 hproper X. The explicit (V := univ) lets X : GeometricCurrentOn univ k be accepted, since preimage_univ is rfl. To unfold Y ω, use `show X.toCurrent (affinePullbackTestOn L 0 hproper univ k ω) = X.toCurrent η`. Rewriting with affinePushforward_apply fails, because the term is only well-typed up to that defeq. Then congr 1, Subtype.ext, funext x, rw [hη x], and step 1.]

6. d commutes with the pull-back. For a C^∞ j-form ω, d(L^#ω) = L^#(dω).
- By the chain rule, D(L^#ω)(x)(v) = Dω(Lx)(Lv) ∘ (L,…,L).
- By Simon 1.11, dβ(x)(v₀,…,v_j) = Σ_i (−1)^i Dβ(x)(v_i)(v₀,…,v̂_i,…,v_j).
- Together: d(L^#ω)(x)(v₀,…,v_j) = Σ_i (−1)^i Dω(Lx)(Lv_i)(Lv₀,…,(Lv_i)^,…,Lv_j) = dω(Lx)(Lv₀,…,Lv_j) = (L^#dω)(x)(v₀,…,v_j). This is Simon 1.14 (Mathlib extDeriv_pullback).
With step 1 in degree j + 1, d(L^#ω)(x) = ρ^{j+1} • dω(ρ • x) for every x.
[Lean: exteriorDerivative_affinePullbackForm L 0 h, where h : IsSmoothForm ω is ω.property.1.1; then step 1 with j + 1.]

7. Third conjunct. Let X, Y ∈ GeometricCurrentOn univ (k+1) satisfy Y(ω′) = X(η′) for all test (k+1)-forms ω′, η′ with η′(x) = ρ^{k+1} • ω′(ρ • x) for all x. Let ω, η be test k-forms with η(x) = ρ^k • ω(ρ • x) for all x.
- By step 1, η = L^#ω as forms.
- Put dω := exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ k ω and dη := exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ k η. These are test (k+1)-forms whose underlying forms are the exterior derivatives (exteriorDerivative = extDeriv).
- Since ω is C^∞, step 6 gives dη(x) = d(L^#ω)(x) = ρ^{k+1} • dω(ρ • x) for every x.
- The hypothesis applied to (ω′, η′) := (dω, dη) gives Y(dω) = X(dη).
- By definition of the boundary (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply: T.boundary ω = T(exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ k ω)), Y.boundary ω = Y(dω) = X(dη) = X.boundary η.
[Lean: rw [boundary_apply, boundary_apply]; apply the hypothesis; intro x. Rewrite the underlying form of η as affinePullbackForm L 0 ω (funext, hη, step 1). Change the goal to exteriorDerivative η x = ρ ^ (k+1) • exteriorDerivative ω (ρ • x). Then rw [exteriorDerivative_affinePullbackForm L 0 ω.property.1.1] and close with step 1 in degree k + 1.]

8. Conclusion. Steps 3, 5 and 7 give the three conjuncts for arbitrary N, ρ > 0 and k. ∎
proof_key_steps: Multilinearity gives α(ρv₁,…,ρv_j) = ρ^jα(v), so the pull-back L^#ω by L = ρ·id is x ↦ ρ^jω(ρx) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_smul_univ on affinePullbackForm L 0 ω).
L is a homeomorphism, hence proper. L^#ω is C^∞ with tsupport ⊆ L⁻¹(tsupport ω), which is compact. This is the first conjunct (affinePullbackTestOn; preimage_univ is rfl).

Pull-back is linear and sequentially continuous in the test-form topology, so Y := X∘L^# is a current (affinePushforward with V := univ). The pair property follows from Subtype.ext and the scaling identity. This is the second conjunct.
d commutes with L^# (exteriorDerivative_affinePullbackForm), so dη(x) = ρ^{k+1}dω(ρx). Apply the (k+1)-pair property to (dω, dη) and unfold ∂ via boundary_apply. This is the third conjunct.

subproblems.title: Hausdorff measure under the dilation x ↦ ρx
subproblems.statement: Hausdorff measure under the dilation x ↦ ρx. Let N, k ∈ ℕ and ρ > 0, and let H^k = μHE[k] be the Euclidean k-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^N (Eucl N). The map φ(x) = ρx is a measurable embedding of ℝ^N, and φ is measure preserving from ρ^k·H^k to H^k. That is, φ_#(ρ^k H^k) = H^k: H^k(φ⁻¹B) = ρ^{−k}H^k(B) for every Borel set B, or equivalently H^k(ρE) = ρ^k H^k(E).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N k : ℕ) (ρ : ℝ), 0 < ρ → MeasurableEmbedding (fun x : Eucl N => ρ • x) ∧ MeasurePreserving (fun x : Eucl N => ρ • x) (ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ k) • (μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl N))) (μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl N))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Step 6: ‘H^s(ρE) = ρ^sH^s(E): coverings scale, diam(ρA) = ρ·diam A; the normalizing constant of μHE[s] is a fixed factor’.

Conventions.
- ℝ^N := Eucl N.
- H^k := μHE[k], Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure, a fixed positive multiple of μH[k].
- φ(x) := ρ • x and c := ENNReal.ofReal(ρ^k).
- Fix N, k and ρ > 0.

1. φ is a homeomorphism of ℝ^N: it is continuous and bijective, with continuous inverse y ↦ ρ⁻¹ • y (ρ ≠ 0).
[Lean: e := Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero ρ hρ.ne'; (⇑e) = (fun x => ρ • x) holds by rfl.]

2. First conjunct. A homeomorphism of Borel spaces is a measurable embedding. It is injective and measurable, and it maps measurable sets to measurable sets: the image of a set is its preimage under the continuous, hence measurable, inverse.
[Lean: e.measurableEmbedding, transported along the rfl equation of step 1.]

3. Scaling law. For r ≠ 0 and every S ⊆ ℝ^N, H^k(r • S) = |r|^k·H^k(S).
- Work first with the unnormalized Hausdorff measure. Any cover {A_i} of S by sets of diameter ≤ δ yields the cover {r • A_i} of r • S, with diam(r • A_i) = |r|·diam A_i ≤ |r|δ and Σ_i diam(r • A_i)^k = |r|^k·Σ_i diam(A_i)^k.
- Taking infima and letting δ ↓ 0 gives H^k(r • S) ≤ |r|^kH^k(S).
- Applying this to r⁻¹ and r • S gives the reverse inequality.
- The normalizing constant of μHE[k] is a common factor.
[Lean: Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀ k (hr : r ≠ 0) S : μHE[k] (r • S) = ‖r‖₊ ^ k • μHE[k] S, in Mathlib/Geometry/Euclidean/Volume/Measure.lean; it needs `open scoped Pointwise` for r • S.]

4. Preimages. For every B ⊆ ℝ^N, φ⁻¹(B) = ρ⁻¹ • B, since ρ • x ∈ B ⟺ x = ρ⁻¹ • (ρ • x) ∈ ρ⁻¹ • B.
[Lean: ext y; Set.mem_smul_set_iff_inv_smul_mem₀ (inv_ne_zero hρ.ne'), inv_inv.]

5. Constant. In [0, ∞], c·(‖ρ⁻¹‖₊^k : [0,∞]) = ENNReal.ofReal(ρ^k·(ρ⁻¹)^k) = ENNReal.ofReal((ρ·ρ⁻¹)^k) = ENNReal.ofReal(1) = 1. This uses ‖ρ⁻¹‖ = ρ⁻¹, valid because ρ > 0.
[Lean: ENNReal.ofReal_coe_nnreal, ENNReal.ofReal_mul (ρ^k ≥ 0), NNReal.coe_pow, coe_nnnorm, Real.norm_of_nonneg, mul_pow, mul_inv_cancel₀, one_pow, ENNReal.ofReal_one.]

6. Second conjunct. φ is measurable by step 2. For every measurable B:
(φ_#(c·H^k))(B) = c·H^k(φ⁻¹(B)) (Measure.map_apply, Measure.smul_apply)
= c·H^k(ρ⁻¹ • B) (step 4)
= c·‖ρ⁻¹‖₊^k·H^k(B) (step 3 with r = ρ⁻¹; ENNReal.smul_def, smul_eq_mul, mul_assoc)
= H^k(B) (step 5).
Two measures that agree on all measurable sets are equal (Measure.ext). So φ_#(c·H^k) = H^k, i.e. MeasurePreserving φ (c·H^k) H^k. Together with step 2 this proves the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: φ(x) = ρ•x is the homeomorphism Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero ρ, hence a measurable embedding.
φ⁻¹(B) = ρ⁻¹•B, and H^k(ρ⁻¹•B) = ‖ρ⁻¹‖₊^k·H^k(B) (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀).
ofReal(ρ^k)·‖ρ⁻¹‖₊^k = 1, so φ_#(ρ^kH^k) and H^k agree on measurable sets; conclude by Measure.ext.

subproblems.title: Mass scales by ρ^k under dilation

[Lean: after rintro _ ⟨ω, hω, rfl⟩, start with `show ENNReal.ofReal (B ω) ≤ _`.]

subproblems.statement: Support scaling under dilation. Let N ∈ ℕ, ρ > 0, k ∈ ℕ, and let X, Y ∈ D_k(ℝ^N) (GeometricCurrentOn univ k on Eucl N). Suppose Y(ω) = X(η) for all test k-forms ω, η with η(x) = ρ^k ω(ρx) for all x. Then spt Y = ρ·spt X, i.e. Y.support = {ρx : x ∈ X.support}.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Steps 3 and 5.
Sibling used: deformation_dilation_calculus, first conjunct (existence of the pull-back test form, for any positive scale).

Conventions and definitions.
- ℝ^N := Eucl N; test forms are elements of TestFormOn univ k.
- SimonGMT Chapter06.CurrentLocalEquality: T.VanishesOn W iff T(ω) = 0 for every test form ω with tsupport ω ⊆ W.
- T.zeroRegion = ⋃₀ {W : IsOpen W ∧ IsCompact (closure W) ∧ closure W ⊆ univ ∧ T.VanishesOn W}.
- T.support = univ ∖ T.zeroRegion.
- For σ > 0, φ_σ(x) := σ • x is a homeomorphism of ℝ^N (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero σ, whose coercion is fun x => σ • x by rfl).
- σ-pair: for A, B ∈ GeometricCurrentOn univ k, (A, B) is a σ-pair if B(ω) = A(η) for all test forms ω, η with η(x) = σ^k • ω(σ • x) for all x.
- By hypothesis, (X, Y) is a ρ-pair.

1. General inclusion. If σ > 0 and (A, B) is a σ-pair, then φ_σ(A.zeroRegion) ⊆ B.zeroRegion. Let x ∈ A.zeroRegion. Choose W with W open, closure W compact, A.VanishesOn W and x ∈ W. Put W′ := φ_σ(W).
(a) W′ is open, since homeomorphisms are open maps (Homeomorph.isOpenMap). closure W′ = φ_σ(closure W) (Homeomorph.image_closure) is compact, as a continuous image of a compact set. Also closure W′ ⊆ univ and σ • x ∈ W′.
(b) B vanishes on W′. Let ω be a test form with tsupport ω ⊆ W′.
- By deformation_dilation_calculus N σ hσ k (first conjunct), there is a test form η with η(y) = σ^k • ω(σ • y) for all y. So η = σ^k • (ω ∘ φ_σ) as forms (funext).
- tsupport η ⊆ tsupport(ω ∘ φ_σ) (tsupport_smul_subset_right).
- tsupport(ω ∘ φ_σ) ⊆ φ_σ⁻¹(tsupport ω) (tsupport_comp_subset_preimage, φ_σ continuous): if ω vanishes near σ • y, then ω ∘ φ_σ vanishes near y.
- φ_σ⁻¹(tsupport ω) ⊆ φ_σ⁻¹(φ_σ(W)) = W, since φ_σ is injective (Function.Injective.mem_set_image).
- A vanishes on W, so A(η) = 0, and B(ω) = A(η) = 0 by the σ-pair property.
By (a) and (b), W′ belongs to the family whose union is B.zeroRegion. Hence σ • x ∈ B.zeroRegion.

2. Inverse pair. (Y, X) is a ρ⁻¹-pair. Take test forms ω′, η′ with η′(x) = (ρ⁻¹)^k • ω′(ρ⁻¹ • x) for all x. Then ρ^k • η′(ρ • x) = ω′(x) for all x (smul_smul, mul_pow, mul_inv_cancel₀, one_pow, one_smul, inv_smul_smul₀). The ρ-pair hypothesis applied to (ω, η) := (η′, ω′) gives Y(η′) = X(ω′).

3. Zero regions.
- Step 1 for (σ, A, B) := (ρ, X, Y) gives φ_ρ(X.zeroRegion) ⊆ Y.zeroRegion.
- Step 1 for (σ, A, B) := (ρ⁻¹, Y, X) is legitimate by step 2, with deformation_dilation_calculus N ρ⁻¹ (inv_pos.2 hρ) k. It gives φ_{ρ⁻¹}(Y.zeroRegion) ⊆ X.zeroRegion.
- So for y ∈ Y.zeroRegion, ρ⁻¹ • y ∈ X.zeroRegion and y = ρ • (ρ⁻¹ • y) (smul_inv_smul₀) ∈ φ_ρ(X.zeroRegion).
- Hence Y.zeroRegion = φ_ρ(X.zeroRegion) (Subset.antisymm).

4. Supports. φ_ρ is bijective (a homeomorphism), so images commute with complements: φ_ρ(Zᶜ) = (φ_ρ(Z))ᶜ (Set.image_compl_eq). Since univ ∖ Z = Zᶜ (Set.compl_eq_univ_sdiff):
Y.support = univ ∖ Y.zeroRegion = (φ_ρ(X.zeroRegion))ᶜ = φ_ρ((X.zeroRegion)ᶜ) = φ_ρ(univ ∖ X.zeroRegion) = (fun x => ρ • x) '' X.support. ∎
proof_key_steps: For a σ-pair (A, B): if A vanishes on an open W with compact closure, then B vanishes on σW. The σ-pull-back η of ω (sibling calculus) has tsupport η ⊆ σ⁻¹·tsupport ω ⊆ W. Hence σ·zeroRegion(A) ⊆ zeroRegion(B).
(X, Y) a ρ-pair implies (Y, X) is a ρ⁻¹-pair; the two inclusions give zeroRegion(Y) = ρ·zeroRegion(X).
x ↦ ρx is bijective, so image commutes with complement (Set.image_compl_eq), giving spt Y = ρ·spt X.

Siblings used: deformation_dilation_calculus (first conjunct) and deformation_dilation_hausdorff.

Conventions and definitions (frozen contract).
- ℝ^N := Eucl N, μ := μHE[k], c := ENNReal.ofReal(ρ^k) and φ(x) := ρ • x.
- For F = (z, α) ∈ LatticeFaceIndex k N (z : Fin N → ℤ, α : Fin k ↪o Fin N), put e_α := (j ↦ EuclideanSpace.single (α j) 1).
- latticeFace r F = {x : ∀ i, (i ∈ range α → r·z_i ≤ x_i ∧ x_i ≤ r·(z_i + 1)) ∧ (i ∉ range α → x_i = r·z_i)}.
- latticeFaceAction r F ω = ∫_{x ∈ latticeFace r F} ω(x)(e_α) dμ. This is a Bochner set integral; no integrability is needed below.
- IsLatticeChain r β T iff T(ω) = ∑' F, β F·latticeFaceAction r F ω for every test form ω.

1. Face scaling: latticeFace ρ F = φ(latticeFace 1 F). Coordinates satisfy (ρ • x)_i = ρ·x_i (PiLp.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul).
(⊇) Let x ∈ latticeFace 1 F.
- For i ∈ range α, z_i ≤ x_i ≤ z_i + 1 (as 1·z_i = z_i). Multiplying by ρ > 0 gives ρ·z_i ≤ ρ·x_i ≤ ρ·(z_i + 1) (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left).
- For i ∉ range α, x_i = z_i, so ρ·x_i = ρ·z_i.
Hence ρ • x ∈ latticeFace ρ F.
(⊆) Let y ∈ latticeFace ρ F and x := ρ⁻¹ • y, so φ(x) = y (smul_inv_smul₀).
- For i ∈ range α, ρ·z_i ≤ y_i ≤ ρ·(z_i + 1) gives z_i ≤ ρ⁻¹·y_i ≤ z_i + 1 (le_inv_mul_iff₀, inv_mul_le_iff₀ with ρ > 0).
- For i ∉ range α, ρ⁻¹·y_i = ρ⁻¹·(ρ·z_i) = z_i (inv_mul_cancel_left₀).
So x ∈ latticeFace 1 F.

2. Face action identity. For every k-form ω, latticeFaceAction 1 F (x ↦ ρ^k • ω(ρ • x)) = latticeFaceAction ρ F ω. By deformation_dilation_hausdorff N k ρ hρ, φ is a measurable embedding and MeasurePreserving φ (c·μ) μ. Using step 1 and the unconditional lemmas MeasurePreserving.setIntegral_image_emb, Measure.restrict_smul, integral_smul_measure, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (ρ^k ≥ 0) and integral_const_mul:
latticeFaceAction ρ F ω = ∫_{φ(latticeFace 1 F)} ω(y)(e_α) dμ(y)
= ∫_{latticeFace 1 F} ω(ρ • x)(e_α) d(c·μ)(x)
= ρ^k·∫_{latticeFace 1 F} ω(ρ • x)(e_α) dμ(x)
= ∫_{latticeFace 1 F} ρ^k·ω(ρ • x)(e_α) dμ(x)
= ∫_{latticeFace 1 F} (ρ^k • ω(ρ • x))(e_α) dμ(x)
= latticeFaceAction 1 F (x ↦ ρ^k • ω(ρ • x)).
The second-to-last equality is evaluation of a scalar multiple of a covector; the two integrands agree definitionally.

3. Chains. Assume IsLatticeChain 1 β X and let ω be a test form.
- By deformation_dilation_calculus N ρ hρ k (first conjunct), there is a test form η with η(x) = ρ^k • ω(ρ • x) for all x. So the underlying form of η is x ↦ ρ^k • ω(ρ • x) (funext).
- Then Y(ω) = X(η) (hypothesis) = ∑' F, β F·latticeFaceAction 1 F η (IsLatticeChain 1 β X at η).
- By step 2, the two summand families are equal as functions of F (congr 1; funext F), so their tsums are equal; no summability is needed. Hence Y(ω) = ∑' F, β F·latticeFaceAction ρ F ω.
As ω is arbitrary, IsLatticeChain ρ β Y. If k > N the index type is empty and both sums vanish; the argument needs no case split. ∎
